advisories.finding: Decision 12 requires a later recording-hygiene entry to annotate COORD, but does not say what authority that act rides. It is not one of D-132's five enumerated authorizations, which cover the file-12 recording, this D-056 successor, the D-002 successor, the MF-6 file-08 edit, and the later authoring. On the corpus's own precedent the act rides ordinary D-000 recording hygiene — D-087 was exactly a COORD hygiene entry adopted on its own cycle without a special user grant, as were D-004 and D-070 for their surfaces.
advisories.whyNotBlocking: Decision 12 already requires the later act to run its own D-000 cycle and commit, which is the operative safeguard. Naming the precedent adds clarity for whoever drafts it; its absence creates no permission and no gap.
advisories.suggestion: When the later entry is drafted, state on its face that it rides ordinary D-000 recording hygiene on the D-087 precedent and not D-132's grant, so no reader infers that the architecture-completion grant reaches COORD content.

Custody is intact across all three turns: turn-3 subject 0fc51c4e at 0444 unmoved, turn-1 e548bd46 and turn-2 42922837 both frozen, HEAD never left d3efe3c, governing tree clean, and all ten measured-inputs rows reproduce exactly including every prior-turn verdict file. That the annotation was not performed is measured, not accepted on the entry's word — COORD holds 741fdc73 with a clean tree at both ends. Because the body is unchanged, both earlier findings could only un-land if the corpus beneath them moved, so I re-derived both from live bytes rather than assume: the two superseded COORD sentences still quote byte-exactly, all five quotations from D-056's pinned subject still reproduce, the D-087 attribution still verifies at commit 953b231, and 'D-056 Class A is not opened' is still present in twelve of twelve recordings. Both advisory dispositions are honest rather than evasive, and one of them fairly rebuts me: on re-reading, the D-131 parenthetical supports only the proposition that later entries read D-056 in COORD, which my turn-2 advisory over-read. The two advisories I leave are that Decision 12 does not name the authority its owed act rides — ordinary D-000 hygiene on the D-087 precedent, not D-132's grant — and that the turn-1 identifier CLAUDE-D133-ADV-3 is never named in any disposition table, though its substance is ruled on at turn 3. Neither creates a permission, a gap, or an unresolved obligation. The entry is ready to adopt.
